title: Smallest Subsequence of Distinct Characters
statement:
From the string `s`, form a subsequence (delete some characters and keep the others in their original order) in which every letter that occurs anywhere in `s` appears exactly once: no letter of `s` may be missing and none may be repeated.

Of all subsequences with that property, return the one that is smallest in lexicographic (dictionary) order.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Build the answer left to right and keep it as small as possible at every step. When a new letter `ch` is smaller than the letter just before it in the answer, it is better to put `ch` earlier, but only if the bigger letter can be taken again later. Knowing the last index of every letter answers that question in O(1), and a stack holds the answer built so far, so letters can be removed from its end. (A slower approach picks the answer one letter at a time: the smallest letter whose first copy still leaves every other needed letter after it.)

## Approach

1. Record `last`, the last index where each letter occurs.
2. Scan `s`. Skip `ch` if it is already in the answer (`used`): its earlier copy is placed at least as well.
3. While the top of `stack` is bigger than `ch` and occurs again after `i`, pop it and unmark it, since a later copy can be used.
4. Push `ch` and mark it as used.
5. The stack, read bottom to top, is the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "bcabc"`, so `last` is `b: 3`, `c: 4`, `a: 2`. Push `b`, then `c` (`stack = [b, c]`). At `i = 2`, `a` is smaller than `c`, and `c` returns at index 4, so pop it; `b` returns at index 3, so pop it too; push `a`. Then push `b` and `c`, giving `"abc"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index of `s` is pushed at most once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the output: the stack, set and map hold at most 26 letters.

## Pitfalls

- Never pop a letter whose last copy has already passed; it would vanish from the answer.
- Skip letters already on the stack; pushing them again breaks "exactly once".
- When popping, remove the letter from `used` so its later copy can be pushed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `last` | last index of each letter in `s` |
| `stack` | the answer built so far, smallest possible prefix |
| `used` | letters currently in `stack` |
| `i`, `ch` | current index and its letter |

narration.2: Prepare a map from each letter to its last position.
narration.4: Later positions overwrite earlier ones, so the map ends with each letter's last index.
narration.6: The stack holds the answer built so far.
narration.7: Track which letters are already in the stack.
narration.9: Scan the string from left to right.
narration.11: This letter is already in the answer at a position at least as good...
narration.14: A bigger letter on top that appears again later can be dropped now and taken from its later copy.
narration.15: Pop it and mark it as no longer in the answer.
narration.17: Place the current letter after everything that stays.
narration.20: The stack from bottom to top is the smallest valid subsequence.
